plan.topic: Tirzepatide and hair loss: how common shedding is and why it's usually temporary (Med Sci (Basel) systematic review of skin side effects, Oct 9, 2026)
plan.angle:
08:00 calm 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short, 60–85 s, 170 words or fewer.

Open within 10 s: 'Hairbrush looking fuller on tirzepatide? Hair shedding has been reported, and it's often temporary shedding linked to fast weight loss (telogen effluvium).'

Use the review's verified findings only, scoped to the drugs it covered (semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide). Give any trial rates per arm against placebo, exactly as published. Observational relative risks get 'linked to' and their absolute context.

What helps: enough protein (with the kidney caveat), and ask your doctor about checking iron, thyroid and vitamin D. See a dermatologist if shedding lasts more than about 6 months, comes in patches, or is painful. No supplement promises.

One GI line. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice' plus the prescriber line. End with 'follow for more'. No emoji, captions mix at 0.02 or lower.

package.title: Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It, Really? #shorts
package.description:
Noticing more hair in the brush on tirzepatide? In its weight-loss trials, hair loss was reported in about 4–5% on the drug vs 1% on placebo. Experts think it's often a temporary shed. Most common side effects are gut ones: nausea, diarrhea, constipation.

Not personal advice. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources: Zepbound Prescribing Information (FDA label); American Academy of Dermatology; NHS.

social.instagram_caption:
That shower drain moment made you panic? Fair.

Here's what's actually known about hair shedding on tirzepatide:

- In tirzepatide's weight-loss trials, hair loss was reported in about 4–5% of people on the drug vs 1% on placebo — roughly 1 in 20
- Experts think it's often telogen effluvium, a temporary shed linked to big weight loss
- It usually shows up a few months after the trigger, and hair tends to regain fullness within 6–9 months
- Enough protein can help (ask your prescriber first if you have kidney disease), and low iron can play a role — worth asking your doctor to check
- Skip the supplement promises
- The most common tirzepatide side effects are gut-related: nausea, diarrhea, constipation

Save this for the next time your hairbrush looks fuller.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe. The per-arm figure (tirzepatide 4–5% depending on dose vs placebo 1%) matches what's reported from the Zepbound label, which pools two placebo-controlled SURMOUNT trials in adults with obesity or overweight. I couldn't parse the label PDF text directly, but several secondary sources quoting the label agree on the figures. The AAD shedding page supports what the script says about telogen effluvium: weight loss of 20 lb or more can trigger it, it shows up a few months later, and fullness tends to return within 6–9 months. It also supports the advice to see a dermatologist if worried. AAD's "18 causes" page supports protein and iron (too little biotin, iron, protein or zinc can cause hair loss). The NHS page lists weight loss and iron deficiency as temporary causes and says to see a GP if worried. Safety lines are present: the kidney-disease caveat on protein, don't stop or change medicines, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line. The word count is about 150. Only minor polish below: the hook is ambiguous, the s2 attribution should be more precise, and there's an optional muted-viewer scope fix and one side-effect framing tweak.

issues.problem: Ambiguous. A 'fuller' hairbrush could be heard as hair looking fuller, the opposite of shedding. That weakens the recognition hook and the loop payoff.
issues.fix: s1 narration: "More hair in your brush on tirzepatide? Here's what's known." s8 narration: "Follow for more. Next time there's extra hair in your brush, you'll know why." s8 on-screen: "Extra hair in your brush? Now you know why"

issues.claim: Experts think it's often telogen effluvium: a temporary shed linked to big weight loss.
issues.problem: The tagged source (AAD) doesn't discuss tirzepatide. It says losing 20 pounds or more can trigger excessive shedding (telogen effluvium). 'Experts think it's often' is vague attribution. Tie the line to what the source actually says.
issues.fix: Narration: "That shower moment feels scary, and that's fair. Dermatologists note that losing twenty pounds or more can trigger telogen effluvium: a temporary shed. It's thought to explain much of it." Keep the on-screen text "Often a temporary shed".

issues.problem: Muted-viewer test: the on-screen card doesn't name the population or the type of trial.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Tirzepatide 4–5% vs placebo 1% (obesity trials, up to 72 wks)". Optional added fact for narration: "It was reported more often in women than men."

issues.claim: Most common side effects? Gut ones: nausea, diarrhea, constipation.
issues.problem: The label's most-common list (≥5%) also includes vomiting, and it includes hair loss itself. As written, the line could imply hair loss isn't a common side effect.
issues.fix: "Most common side effects are gut ones: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation. Hair loss is on the label's list too." Keep the rest of s7 unchanged.
